payload.summary: Fix two bugs so report totals match order totals: (1) pricing.py apply_discount currently multiplies by (1 + discount) instead of (1 - discount); (2) report.py summarize hardcodes a 10% discount (price * 0.9) and ignores the discount/tax_rate parameters instead of delegating to pricing.final_price. After fixes, both order_total and summarize should compute item price as price * (1 - discount) * (1 + tax_rate), matching tests/test_shop.py.

tasks.title: Fix apply_discount formula in pricing.py
tasks.description: In pricing.py, change the return statement of apply_discount from `price * (1 + discount)` to `price * (1 - discount)` so a discount fraction correctly reduces the price. Keep the existing ValueError bounds check for discount in [0, 1). This makes apply_discount(100, 0.2) == 80.0.

tasks.title: Fix report.py summarize to use final_price
tasks.description: In report.py, replace the hardcoded `prices = [i["price"] * 0.9 for i in items]` with `prices = [final_price(i["price"], discount, tax_rate) for i in items]` so summarize honors the passed discount and tax_rate and matches order totals. The `from pricing import final_price` import already exists at the top.

tasks.title: Verify behavior with tests
tasks.description: Run tests/test_shop.py (or the project test runner) and confirm all assertions pass, especially test_discount (80.0), test_final_price (88.0), test_order_total (132.0), test_order_coupon (78.0), and test_summarize (total 132.0, average 66.0, max_price 88.0). If tests are not present/run externally, manually verify apply_discount(100, 0.2)==80.0 and summarize([{"price":100},{"price":50}], discount=0.2, tax_rate=0.1)["total"]==132.0.

findings: pricing.py apply_discount (lines 4-8) returns `price * (1 + discount)`; for discount=0.2 and price=100 this yields 120.0 instead of the expected 80.0. The formula should be `price * (1 - discount)`.

report.py summarize (lines 5-12) hardcodes `prices = [i["price"] * 0.9 for i in items]`, ignoring its `discount` and `tax_rate` parameters. It should compute each item price via `final_price(i["price"], discount, tax_rate)`.
order.py order_total (lines 5-9) correctly delegates to pricing.final_price, so once pricing.py is fixed order totals become correct; report.py is the remaining mismatch.

tests/test_shop.py already encodes the expected behavior: apply_discount(100,0.2)==80.0, final_price(100,0.2,0.1)==88.0, order_total([100,50],0.2,0.1)==132.0, order_total coupon ==78.0, and summarize total/average/max_price ==132.0/66.0/88.0.

changes: pricing.py apply_discount now returns price * (1 - discount) instead of price * (1 + discount)
report.py summarize now computes prices via final_price(i["price"], discount, tax_rate) instead of hardcoded i["price"] * 0.9
